doe-osti-3423231-thiol-ene-dextran-based:
Lawrence Livermore report LLNL-TR-2023278, by N. Goshi and dated August 2026, builds soft hydrogels to hold living neurons in three dimensions. The gels use dextran linked by thiol-ene chemistry, set with light. A soft, water-rich home lets nerve cells grow in lab studies.

Gel strength was measured before and after setting. The light-set gel left its even-flow range at 0.318 percent strain in the test shown. Mass loss was tracked as enzymes broke the gel down over days. Fresh enzyme solution replaced old every 2 to 3 days. Brain researchers gain a tunable cell home with known limits.
